explanation: Turkish hospitality strongly favors the host serving and offering drinks, and refusing or bypassing an offer can read as rejecting the host's welcome. Pouring your own drink at a restaurant table is not a documented grave insult, but it can seem impatient or as if you are not letting others play host. The sources do not directly address self-pouring, so this is inferred from broader hospitality norms.
local_tip: Let your host or the server pour first, and if you want more, offer to pour for others before filling your own glass.

also_check.note: Pouring for others is the norm; filling your own glass can seem slightly self-focused.
The tamada or host leads toasts and pouring; self-pouring can disrupt the ritual.
Elders and hosts pour; pouring your own drink is often seen as a sign that others are neglecting you.

sources.title: Turkish Etiquette: The Cultural Guide I Wish I Had Before My First Day in Turkey
